name: Math · Roots of unity & complex numbers

hook.text: Six numbers whose sixth power is 1

youtube.title: The 6 roots of z⁶ = 1 make a hexagon ⬡ #shorts
youtube.description:
The solutions of z⁶ = 1 are the six points e^(2πik/6) on the unit circle. They split the circle into six equal arcs and join into a regular hexagon. One note for each root.

hook.text: What do the roots of z^n = 1 look like?

youtube.title: Roots of unity: n from 3 to 12 📐 #shorts
youtube.description:
z³ = 1 gives a triangle, z⁴ = 1 a square, z⁵ = 1 a pentagon … every n gives a regular polygon. More roots, more notes: each polygon plays its own scale.

hook.text: Only some roots can build all the others

youtube.title: Primitive roots of unity: 4 of 12 light up ✨ #shorts
youtube.description:
A root e^(2πik/12) is primitive when its powers reach every other root: that happens exactly when k and 12 share no factor. For n = 12 that is k = 1, 5, 7, 11 (gold): φ(12) = 4.

Which one should I do next? 👇

#shorts

presets.name: Powers of a Root: a 7-Point Star

youtube.title: The powers of one root draw a star ⭐ #shorts
youtube.description:
Let ω = e^(2πi·3/7). Its powers ω, ω², ω³ … jump 3 places each time and draw the star polygon {7/3}. After 7 steps it is back at 1 having visited every root: it generates them all.

Which one should I do next? 👇

#shorts

presets.name: Which Step Sizes Reach Every Root? (n = 12)

youtube.title: Step size and symmetry: only 1, 5, 7 and 11 reach all 12 🔢 #shorts
youtube.description:
Jump m places round 12 points. If m and 12 share a factor you get stuck in a smaller polygon (m = 6: just 2 points!). Only m = 1, 5, 7, 11 visit all 12: the numbers coprime to 12.

presets.name: Multiply by i: a Quarter Turn

hook.text: What does multiplying by i do?

youtube.title: Multiplying by i turns a point 90° 🔄 #shorts
youtube.description:
Multiply any complex number by i and it turns a quarter turn: 1 → i → −1 → −i → 1. Four times and you are back: i⁴ = 1.

hook.text: Turn a little, shrink a little

youtube.title: Multiply by 0.93·e^(i·25°) and a spiral appears 🌀 #shorts
youtube.description:
Multiplication by ρ·e^(iφ) turns by φ and scales by ρ. Do it again and again and the points follow a logarithmic spiral: the shape of shells and galaxies.

presets.name: The Roots Always Add Up to Zero

hook.text: Add the roots. What is left?

youtube.title: The roots of unity always add up to 0 ➕ #shorts
youtube.description:
1 + ω + ω² + … + ω^(n−1) = 0. Put the vectors head to tail and they walk round a regular polygon and end exactly where they started. Try n = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

hook.text: The most beautiful equation in maths

youtube.title: Euler’s identity e^(iπ) + 1 = 0 🤯 #shorts
youtube.description:
e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ is a point going round the unit circle. After half a turn (θ = π) it lands on −1: e^(iπ) = −1. Two notes play the horizontal and vertical shadows of the point.

hook.text: Sine and cosine are shadows of one point

youtube.title: Sine and cosine are two shadows of one turning point 🎡 #shorts
youtube.description:
A point at angle θ on the unit circle has x = cos θ and y = sin θ. Its shadow on the horizontal axis plays one note, its shadow on the vertical axis another: you hear the two waves.
